questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: Which feature of capitalism is emphasized in the textbook?
options: Most means of production are privately owned
All production is controlled by government
Prices are fixed by a central plan
Land is owned only by workers
questions.answer: Most means of production are privately owned
questions.explanation: The textbook explains that most means of production are privately owned in a capitalist system.
questions.sourceNote: History Unit 1, §1.1 Features of Capitalism, extraction lines 329–336

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: In which country did the Industrial Revolution first begin according to the textbook?
questions.explanation: The source states that the Industrial Revolution first started in England in the eighteenth century.
questions.sourceNote: History Unit 1, §1.1 Features of Capitalism, extraction lines 329–336

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: Which energy sources replaced wind and water power after the Industrial Revolution?
questions.explanation: The textbook identifies coal and steam as new sources of energy and power that replaced wind and water.
questions.sourceNote: History Unit 1, §1.1 Features of Capitalism, extraction lines 337–342

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: What system replaced the domestic system during industrialization?
questions.explanation: The source says the factory system was created to replace domestic production in homes or workshops.
questions.sourceNote: History Unit 1, §1.1 Features of Capitalism, extraction lines 337–342

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: What two social classes did industrialization especially promote?
questions.explanation: The textbook identifies the proletariat and bourgeoisie as new socio-economic classes promoted by industrialization.
questions.sourceNote: History Unit 1, §1.1 Features of Capitalism, extraction lines 337–342

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: In the capitalist system, what do proletarians receive for their labour?
questions.explanation: The source states that proletarians receive wages for their labour.
questions.sourceNote: History Unit 1, §1.1 Features of Capitalism, extraction lines 360–368

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: What does the textbook call an economy in which government controls production, distribution, and prices?
questions.explanation: The source defines a command economy as one in which government controls production, distribution, and prices.
questions.sourceNote: History Unit 1, §1.1 Features of Capitalism, extraction lines 360–368

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: How does the textbook define nationalism?
options: A feeling of belonging and loyalty to a nation
A system of government price controls
questions.answer: A feeling of belonging and loyalty to a nation
questions.explanation: Nationalism is described as a feeling of belonging and loyalty that makes people think of themselves as a nation.
questions.sourceNote: History Unit 1, §1.2 Features of Nationalism, extraction lines 438–449

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: What was a main objective of the Treaty of Vienna in 1815?
options: To restore monarchies and reverse Napoleonic changes
To abolish slavery in the United States
To unite Italy under a republic
questions.answer: To restore monarchies and reverse Napoleonic changes
questions.explanation: Britain, Russia, Prussia, and Austria drew the Treaty of Vienna to reverse Napoleonic changes and restore monarchies.
questions.sourceNote: History Unit 1, §1.2 Features of Nationalism, extraction lines 452–457

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: Which power occupied Lombardy and Venice before Italian unification?
questions.explanation: Austrian occupation of Lombardy and Venice was listed as an obstacle to Italian unity.
questions.sourceNote: History Unit 1, §1.2.1 Unification of Italy, extraction lines 501–517

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: Which movement did Giuseppe Mazzini found in 1831?

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: What position did Count Camillo di Cavour hold from 1852?
options: Prime minister of the Kingdom of Sardinia

questions.explanation: Cavour became prime minister of the independent Kingdom of Sardinia in 1852.
questions.sourceNote: History Unit 1, §1.2.1 Unification of Italy, extraction lines 559–568

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: What force did Giuseppe Garibaldi lead in southern Italy?

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: Who became king when the Kingdom of Italy was established in 1861?

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: What was the Zollverein?

A military alliance led by France
A treaty that created the League of Nations
questions.answer: An economic alliance that removed tariffs between German states
questions.explanation: The Zollverein was a customs union that promoted trade by removing tariffs among German states.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: Which three wars did Bismarck use in the unification of Germany?

Seven Weeks, World War I, and World War II
questions.answer: Danish, Seven Weeks, and Franco-Prussian wars
questions.explanation: The text lists the Danish War, Seven Weeks War, and Franco-Prussian War as the three wars of German unification.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: Which groups fought in the American Civil War according to the textbook?

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: What combination created the Eastern Question?

Industrialization, free trade, and factory growth
American secession, abolitionism, and cotton production
questions.answer: Balkan nationalism, Ottoman decline, and competing Great Power interests
questions.explanation: The Eastern Question arose from Balkan nationalism, the declining Ottoman Empire, and divergent interests of Great Powers.
questions.sourceNote: History Unit 1, §1.2.4 Nationalism and the Eastern Question, extraction lines 928–931

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914
questions.question: Capitalist enterprises are mainly run by a command economic system.
questions.explanation: Capitalism is distinguished from a command economy because its means of production are mainly privately owned and government interferes less.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914

questions.question: Britain supported the Balkan nationalists because it wanted Russia in the Mediterranean.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815 to 1914

questions.sourceNote: History Unit 1, §1.1 Features of Capitalism, extraction lines 337–342
